cards.text: Paul, an apostle, is writing to the church of God in Corinth (1 Corinthians 1:1-2). They wrote to him about some matters, and now he's taking up the matters they wrote about. His opening line: "It is good to abstain from sexual relations."

cards.question: Paul says it's good to abstain from sexual relations. But because there is so much sexual immorality, what does he say each man and each woman should have?

answers.text: A spouse of their own
An elder to watch over them
A set day of fasting

cards.text: Now Paul gets into married life. I've never been married, friend, and sharing a junk drawer with a twist tie for years does NOT count.

cards.question: Paul talks about marital duty in a marriage. Who does he say should fulfill it?

answers.text: The husband and the wife both
The husband and not the wife
The wife and not the husband

cards.question: Paul says the husband has authority over his wife's body, and likewise the wife has authority over her husband's body.

answers.text: True
False

cards.question: Paul tells married couples not to deprive each other, with one exception. What is it?

answers.text: By mutual consent for a time of prayer
When one of them is away on a journey
During the days of a feast

cards.question: After that time of prayer, Paul says the couple should come together again. Why?

answers.text: So Satan won't tempt them
So the church won't worry
So the house won't feel empty

cards.question: Paul adds a note about how he means what he's just said. How does he say it?

answers.text: As a concession not a command
As a rule from the elders
As a warning from the prophets

cards.text: Then Paul says, "I wish that all men were as I am."

cards.question: Right after Paul says he wishes all men were as he is, he adds a "but." What does he say?

answers.text: Each one has his own gift from God
Most people won't follow his example
Only apostles are called to be that way

cards.text: Now Paul turns to a new group: the unmarried and widows.

cards.question: What does Paul say is good for the unmarried and widows?

answers.text: To remain unmarried as he is
To marry as soon as they can
To move back with their families

cards.question: Paul says that even if the unmarried and widows cannot control themselves, they should still stay unmarried.

answers.text: True
False

cards.text: Paul's line on it: "For it is better to marry than to burn with passion." Next, he turns to the married, and he says this command is not from him but from the Lord.

cards.question: Paul gives the married a command from the Lord. What does it say about a wife?

answers.text: She must not separate from her husband
She must pray for her husband daily
She must keep her husband's customs

cards.question: And if a wife does separate from her husband, Paul gives her two options. What are they?

answers.text: Stay unmarried or be reconciled to him
Remarry or go back to her family
Wait a year or ask the elders

cards.question: Paul says the husband has a command here too: he must not divorce his wife.

answers.text: True
False

cards.text: Then Paul speaks to the rest. And right up front, he labels where this next part comes from.

cards.question: Paul said his command to the married came from the Lord, not him. How does he label this next part, to the rest?

answers.text: From Paul himself not the Lord
From the Lord just like before
From the apostles in Jerusalem

cards.text: Here's his case: a believer married to someone who doesn't believe. Brother or sister, Paul covers both.

cards.question: A believer's spouse doesn't believe, but is willing to live with them. What does Paul say the believer must do?

answers.text: Stay and not divorce them
Wait for them to believe first
Bring the matter to the elders

cards.question: Paul gives a reason the believer should stay in a marriage with an unbeliever. What is it?

answers.text: The unbeliever is sanctified through them
The church needs every family it has
The Law of Moses requires it of them

cards.question: Paul says that because of this, the children in that home are holy, not unclean.

answers.text: True
False

cards.text: But what if the unbelieving spouse doesn't stay? What if they leave?

cards.question: If the unbelieving spouse leaves, what does Paul say?

answers.text: Let them go and the believer isn't bound
Follow them until they come back
Ask the church to bring them back

cards.text: Then Paul says, "God has called you to live in peace." And he follows it with two questions, one for a wife and one for a husband.

cards.question: Paul asks a believing wife and a believing husband the same kind of question. What is it?

answers.text: How do you know whether you'll save your spouse
Why did you marry someone who doesn't believe
Have you prayed for your spouse today

cards.text: Now Paul zooms out from marriage to everybody. Each one should lead the life the Lord has assigned to him, the one God has called him to.

cards.question: Paul says leading the life God called you to is something he prescribes only for the church in Corinth.

answers.text: True
False

cards.text: ALL the churches. Same recipe, every kitchen, no special batch just for Corinth. Then Paul gives an example: circumcision.

cards.question: A man was already circumcised when God called him. What does Paul say he should do about it?

answers.text: Stay just as he was
Bring an offering for it
Confess it to the church

cards.question: If a man was still uncircumcised when God called him, Paul says he should get circumcised.

answers.text: True
False

cards.text: Then Paul says, "Circumcision is nothing and uncircumcision is nothing." Both of them. NOTHING. Knocked flat in one sentence.

cards.question: If circumcision and uncircumcision are both nothing, what does Paul say counts?

answers.text: Keeping God's commandments
Where a man was born
Knowing the most Scripture

cards.text: Paul sums it up: each one should remain in the situation he was in when he was called. Then he gets to a harder case, someone who was a slave when God called him.

cards.question: What does Paul tell someone who was a slave when God called him?

answers.text: Don't let it concern you but take freedom if you can
Run away from your master as soon as you can
Stay a slave even if you're offered your freedom

cards.question: Paul flips it around. The one who was a slave when called by the Lord is the Lord's ___. The one who was free when called is Christ's ___.

answers.text: freedman
slave
son
guest
steward

cards.text: Then Paul says, "You were bought at a price; do not become slaves of men." He told them they were bought at a price just a little earlier too, in 1 Corinthians 6:20.

And Paul lands it one more time: "Brothers, each one should remain in the situation he was in when God called him." But friend, Paul's still got their letter in his hand, and this conversation is NOT over.
